{"answers":[{"question_id":"Q024_fibronectin_fragment_selection","answer":"In SCOPe 2.08, d1o5dt2 (SUNID 103884; 1o5d T:107–205) has a domain-specific “fr” annotation: missing more than one-third of the common structure and/or sequence. It remains classified in fibronectin type III family b.1.2.1; the flag concerns completeness, not exclusion from the family. d1uc6a1 (SUNID 107766; 1uc6 A:6–109) has no corresponding fragment annotation.

For alignment, compare the homologous residues actually present, using the shared structural core and reporting coverage alongside sequence identity or structural similarity. Treat absent regions as missing information, not automatically as evolutionary deletions or highly divergent sequence. Check deposited sequence, observed coordinates, and residue mapping to distinguish construct truncation from unresolved residues and identify the missing elements; the annotated residue ranges alone cannot establish completeness. A good fit over the fragment does not demonstrate agreement across the entire domain.

For a general family representative or full-domain modeling template, prefer a verified complete, well-resolved member. Between these two, d1uc6a1 is the provisional choice on completeness grounds, but absence of a fragment flag does not establish superior experimental quality. Retain d1o5dt2 for tissue-factor-specific comparisons or local templates where its observed region is relevant; it cannot supply coordinates or interactions for missing regions.

Both belong to family b.1.2.1 within fibronectin type III superfamily b.1.2, supporting common ancestry. Fold b.1, immunoglobulin-like beta-sandwich, describes broader structural similarity without by itself establishing homology; class b denotes all-beta proteins. d1uc6a1 represents ciliary neurotrophic factor receptor alpha, whereas d1o5dt2 represents human tissue factor’s extracellular region. Their shared family does not justify transferring receptor or coagulation functions. Preserve this genuine biological diversity, but do not count fragment-induced missing strands, contacts, or apparent shortening as a new family architecture.
